title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Orientation day on campus.


About a month ago, I landed in Vancouver to begin UBC’s Master of Data Science program, and orientation week already feels like a blur. Between campus tours, software installations, and figuring out bus routes, the moment that stayed with me most was meeting my cohort.
Coming from an education background, I was not entirely sure what to expect. I have often thought of myself as a bit of a loner, but a few conversations in that room quickly changed the story. I found myself surrounded by people with rich and diverse experiences, all drawn here by a shared goal: making sense of data and using it to do something meaningful.
The first week of classes moved quickly—lectures, labs, and readings piled up before I had even fully unpacked. The pace was not a surprise; I had heard that the MDS program moves fast. What did surprise me was how collaborative it already feels. People are troubleshooting code together, comparing notes after class, and forming study groups.
If I am honest, I am still adjusting. A new city, a new academic rhythm, and new people all at once can feel overwhelming, and there is a quiet hum of nerves beneath the excitement. But I would rather feel that in week one than pretend I already have everything figured out.
More to come as the program picks up.

title: About
text: I grew up and studied in Ghana, earning a BSc in Information and Communication Technology Education from the University of Education, Winneba, with First Class Honours. For the past decade I’ve worked as an ICT teacher and IT Coordinator at Agotime Senior High School, part of the Ghana Education Service — teaching Mathematics, Statistics, Probability, and ICT, managing school MIS systems, and supporting information security processes. Alongside teaching, I’ve co-founded and led community initiatives focused on expanding ICT access for rural and underserved youth, and on building entrepreneurship skills among young people.

title: About
text:
Why Data Science
Years of working with school data — attendance, performance, resource allocation — showed me how much untapped potential there is in applying rigorous analysis to education systems. I’m drawn to UBC’s Master of Data Science for its interdisciplinary blend of statistics and computer science, and I’m especially looking forward to diving into data workflows, statistical inference, and the industry capstone. My goal is to bring these skills back to Ghana’s education sector — building data pipelines and analytics that can support better resource allocation, teacher development, and student outcomes.

title: About
text:
Outside of Data Science
Beyond the classroom and the code, I care a lot about community and service — from leadership roles in student associations to volunteering with education and health outreach projects. I also enjoy sharing educational content on sustainability and the SDGs online, and I have a long-standing interest in how environmental issues affect communities back home. On weekends, you’ll usually find me exploring something new, whether that’s an idea, a place, or a skill.
